thread:
Sam: Heads up — after today's runtime push we're seeing p99 tail latency jumps on the continuous-batcher pools. p50/p95/p99 went from 18/42/130ms -> 20/58/620ms for short seq (<=128). Rolling window: 12:10-12:30 UTC. Anyone oncall? https://dash.redwood.ai/teams/eng-runtime/queries/xyz

Lee: Oof. Any config changes in admission control or microbatcher? What was in the deploy?

Sam: Deployed commit 7f3a2b4: "admission: dynamic-target-size heuristic" + kernel selector tweak (prefer fused-kernel v2). Kernel logs show frequent fallbacks. Pasting tail of logs: 

Sam: ```
[12:12:03] kernel_selector: picked fused-v2 for model:mistral-7b seq:64 backend:triton
[12:12:03] kernel_selector: fallback -> generic-cuda because workspace alloc failed
[12:12:04] admission: microbatch_size recompute: from 16 -> 6 (pressure high)
[12:12:07] kvcache: hit_rate 0.76 -> 0.41 for shard s-34
[12:12:07] kvcache: eviction_count +128 in 10s (compaction triggered)
```

Izzy: KV cache hit drop is suspicious — eviction policy changed last week? We had a compaction cron at 11:50 UTC that touches the same shards.

Taylor: Quick check — can we repro locally with loadgen? I can spin up a test cluster with the same commit and synthetic traffic.

Sam: @ci-bot can you show the rollout diff for 7f3a2b4?

ci-bot: Rollout 7f3a2b4 applied to pool:continuous-batcher (20 nodes). Changed files: runtime/admission.cpp, runtime/kernel_selector.py, runtime/kv_cache.cc. Triggered at 12:08:11 UTC.

Lee: Hypothesis: kernel fallbacks increase latency variance and reduce effective batching (less packing), admission auto-shrinks microbatches, compaction causes kvcache hits to drop -> combined effect skyrockets tail latency.

Izzy: Correlated metric: eviction_count spike at 12:11:50 on shard s-34 exactly when p99 jumps. Suggest disabling compaction on continuous-batcher pool as quick mitigation.

Sam: Can we rollback kernel selector change only? How invasive is that?

Taylor: Kernel selector change is a config/logic tweak in userland (runtime/kernel_selector.py) — low-risk revert and fast build. I can push revert to canary.

Lee: In parallel, add a conservative admission guard: if kvcache_hit_rate < 0.6 then prevent microbatch auto-shrink. Quick patch suggestion: 

Lee: ```
// admission guard to avoid pathological shrink during kvcache churn
if (kvcache.hit_rate() < 0.6) {
  admission.set_min_batch(8);
  admission.disable_dynamic_shrink();
}
```

Sam: Rolling Lee's hotfix to 3 canaries now (patch 7f3a2b7).

Sam: Canary metrics after hotfix: p99 on canary nodes went from 620ms -> 170ms, p95 from 58ms -> 46ms. Throughput unaffected.

Izzy: With hotfix stabilizing canary, we should still schedule a deeper profiling run: NVTX ranges, memory alloc traces, and perf counters targeted at kernel selection paths. I'll capture GPU memalloc failure patterns.

Taylor: I'll push the kernel_selector revert to canary (patch 7f3a2b6) and run loadgen against canary for 20 minutes.

Sam: Filing follow-ups: (1) Taylor to revert kernel_selector tweak and validate (owner: Taylor) (2) Izzy to investigate compaction/eviction thresholds and propose durable fix (owner: Izzy) (3) Lee to formalize admission guard and add automated alert on hit_rate drop (owner: Lee).

Taylor: ack, creating PRs and linking them here once green.

Izzy: I'll also upload a perf trace to S3: s3://redwood-perf/2026-03-18/2319876543-trace.tar.gz and add notes to incident ticket.

Sam: Nice work team. Can we add a short runbook entry: if p99 > 300ms and kvcache.hit_rate < 0.6 then roll canary patch + disable compaction?

Lee: Yep, I'll add to runbook and set a pager alert threshold.

Sam: Thanks — closing the immediate loop. :thumbsup:
